title: Notes on Learning to Cook From Scratch
script: Narrator: [honestly] Three months ago, I could barely fry an egg without setting off the smoke alarm, which honestly says a lot about where I started.
Narrator: I decided to learn cooking properly because I was tired of spending most of my salary on takeout every single week.
Narrator: [amused] My first attempt was a simple soup, and somehow I still managed to burn it, even though soup is mostly just water and patience.
Narrator: [determined] Instead of giving up, I watched a few videos, read some old recipes my grandmother had written by hand, and tried again the next day.
Narrator: [proud] That second soup was actually edible, and I remember feeling proud of something so small in a way I hadn't expected.
Narrator: After that, I gave myself one simple rule, cook something new every weekend, even if it turns out badly the first time.
Narrator: [laughing] Some weekends were disasters. I once made rice so dry it could barely be called rice, and I laughed about it for days afterward.
Narrator: [pleased] But slowly, my kitchen stopped feeling like a scary, unfamiliar room and started feeling like somewhere I actually enjoyed spending time.
Narrator: [practical] I learned that basic seasoning and patient practice matter more than expensive ingredients, while food-safety steps and important recipe measurements still need care.
Narrator: Now, when friends come over, I actually cook for them instead of ordering food, which still feels like a strange, wonderful change.
Narrator: [warmly] My mother laughed when I told her this, because she remembers me refusing to enter the kitchen as a teenager.
Narrator: I told her that things change when your wallet gets tired of takeout containers piling up in the recycling bin.
Narrator: [reflective] What surprised me most wasn't the cooking itself, but how calming it became after long, stressful days at the office.
Narrator: Chopping vegetables slowly, without rushing, somehow clears my head better than scrolling my phone ever manages to do.

Narrator: [encouraging] If you have never cooked before, start with a simple recipe, read the safety steps first, and allow yourself to learn, because burnt soup taught me more than any perfect meal ever could.
